requirements.title: Write-route gate
requirements.rationale: A write must be refused before it reads or changes anything when the caller may not write or the workspace cannot take a write.

criteria.condition: a write route is called with a PAT that lacks the scope `git:write`
criteria.action: refuse the request without reading the repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`; no ref moves and no event is emitted; the answer is the same whether or not the workspace exists

setup: the write gate of internal/scm with a stub access component and a stub workspace lookup
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/write_test.go: wrap a probe handler in the write gate; send a request with a PAT whose scopes are {git:read}; assert status == 403 and error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert the probe handler did not run; the same request with scopes {git:write} runs the probe; an API key runs the probe

criteria.condition: a write route is called by a caller whose access to the workspace is below write
criteria.action: refuse the request without reading the repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` when the caller has no access to the workspace; HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` when the caller has read access only; no ref moves

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/write_test.go beside the scope test, a table over the access level the stub access component reports {none -> 404 not_found, read -> 403 forbidden, write -> probe runs, owner -> probe runs, admin -> probe runs}: assert status and error.error_type; assert the probe ran only in the last three rows

criteria.condition: a write route is called by a caller with write access on a workspace that is not writable
criteria.action: refuse the request by the workspace's status and leave the repository untouched
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_archived` for an archived workspace, `parent_archived` for a fork whose parent is archived, `workspace_busy` for a workspace (or a fork's parent) that is `pending`, `cloning` or in a reclone, archive or delete, and `workspace_not_ready` for a `failed` workspace

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/write_test.go, a table over the workspace the stub lookup returns {status archived -> 409 workspace_archived; a fork with status ready whose parent is archived -> 409 parent_archived; pending -> 409 workspace_busy; cloning -> 409 workspace_busy; ready with an archive running -> 409 workspace_busy; a fork whose parent is cloning -> 409 workspace_busy; failed -> 409 workspace_not_ready; ready -> probe runs}: assert status and error.error_type; assert the probe ran only for ready

criteria.action: for any of the five write routes (`POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs`, `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name`, `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase`), run the write gate before the route's own validation
criteria.contract: each route answers the gate's refusal (`insufficient_scope`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `workspace_archived`, `parent_archived`, `workspace_busy`, `workspace_not_ready`) and never `invalid_request` when both apply

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
the real router of internal/server with the scm routes registered
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/write_routes_test.go, a table over the five routes, each sent with an empty JSON body {} (which would fail the route's own validation) in three set-ups {PAT with git:read only -> 403 insufficient_scope; org member with read access -> 403 forbidden; owner on an archived workspace -> 409 workspace_archived}: assert status and error.error_type for every route and set-up; assert git for-each-ref output is unchanged after the table

requirements.title: Commit creation and its compare-and-swap
requirements.rationale: An agent commits its edits in one request and is told when the branch moved under it, so it never overwrites work it has not seen (SCM-US-02).

criteria.condition: `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` names an existing branch and an `expected_head_sha` equal to its head
criteria.action: create one commit whose parent is the branch head and whose tree is the parent's tree with the operations applied, and move the branch to it
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with `{commit, branch, change, change_error}`: `commit` is the commit object (40-character `sha`, `parents` holding exactly the old head), `branch` is the ref object at the new commit; `base_ref` is ignored

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
an unprotected branch work at main's head
the caller is the workspace owner with an API key
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go: head = rev-parse('work'); r = post('/workspaces/w/scm/commits', {branch:'work', expected_head_sha: head, message:'m', operations:[put a.txt 'hi']}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.commit.parents == [head]; assert r.json.commit.message == 'm'; assert r.json.branch.name == 'refs/heads/work' and r.json.branch.sha == r.json.commit.sha; assert len(r.json.commit.sha) == 40; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/work == r.json.commit.sha; assert git show work:a.txt == 'hi'; assert 'change' and 'change_error' are present and null; a second row sends base_ref:'nope' together with the right expected_head_sha and still gets 201

criteria.condition: `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` names a branch that does not exist and a `base_ref` that resolves to a commit
criteria.action: create the commit on top of the commit `base_ref` resolves to and create the branch at the new commit
criteria.contract: HTTP 201; `commit.parents` holds exactly the resolved base commit; the branch exists afterwards at `commit.sha`

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table over base_ref {'main', 'refs/heads/main', the full id of main's head, a 7-character prefix of it}: r = post commits {branch:'new-<i>', base_ref, message, operations:[put x 'y']}; assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.commit.parents == [main head]; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/new-<i> == r.json.commit.sha

criteria.action: for any created commit, record the request's `author` name and e-mail as the author, or the caller's name and e-mail when `author` is absent, and the hub's identity as the committer
criteria.contract: `commit.author` and `commit.committer` in the 201 answer, and the same values in the stored commit

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table {author {name:'A', email:'a@x'} given -> commit.author.name == 'A' and email == 'a@x'; author absent, caller user (Kim, kim@x) -> author is Kim; author absent, admin token -> author equals the hub identity}: in every row assert r.json.commit.committer.name and .email equal the hub's configured committer identity and git log -1 --format='%an|%ae|%cn|%ce' agrees with the response

criteria.condition: the named branch exists and `expected_head_sha` is absent or differs from the branch head
criteria.action: refuse the request, create no visible commit and leave the branch where it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_moved` and `error.details.current_sha` equal to the branch's current head; no event is emitted

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/

criteria.condition: the commit request is malformed: `branch` is missing or not a valid branch name, `message` is missing or empty, `operations` holds more than 1,000 entries, `author` lacks `name` or `email`, or the branch does not exist and `base_ref` is absent or resolves to no commit
criteria.action: refuse the request and move no ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`, except HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for a `base_ref` that resolves to no commit; exactly 1,000 operations are accepted

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table over bodies {no branch; branch ''; branch 'a..b'; no message; message ''; operations not an array; 1001 put operations; author without email; branch missing and no base_ref} each -> 400 invalid_request, and {branch missing, base_ref 'no-such-ref'} -> 404 ref_not_found; a body with exactly 1000 put operations -> 201; assert for-each-ref is unchanged after every refused row

criteria.condition: the body of `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` is larger than `[scm].max_commit_size` (default 32 MiB)
criteria.action: refuse the request without parsing it
criteria.contract: HTTP 413 with `error_type` `payload_too_large`; a body at or under the limit is read in full even when it is larger than `[server].max_body_size`

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go: start the routes with max_commit_size = 1024; post a commit body of 2000 bytes -> assert 413 and error.error_type == 'payload_too_large'; post one of 900 bytes -> 201; with the default configuration post a body of 2 MiB (over the 1 MiB default body limit of other routes) -> 201; in internal/config/config_test.go: a file with [scm] max_commit_size = '64MB' loads as 64 MiB and a file without the key loads as 32 MiB

criteria.condition: another write moves the branch between the read of its head and the compare-and-swap of a commit request
criteria.action: answer the loser of the race as moved and leave only the winner's commit reachable from the branch
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_moved` and `details.current_sha`; of several concurrent commit requests with one `expected_head_sha` exactly one answers 201; the losers emit no event and touch no change

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go: start 8 goroutines posting different put operations to branch work with the same expected_head_sha; assert exactly one answer is 201 and seven are 409 with error_type 'ref_moved' and details.current_sha equal to the winner's commit.sha or the old head; assert git rev-list --count old..work == 1; assert the event sink holds events for one commit only

requirements.title: File operations
requirements.rationale: The four operations are the whole vocabulary a client has for describing an edit; each must do one predictable thing or fail the whole request.

criteria.condition: a `put` operation carries a valid `path`, exactly one of `content` (UTF-8 text) and `content_base64`, and no `mode` or a `mode` of `100644`, `100755` or `120000`
criteria.action: create the file at `path`, or replace it, with the given bytes and mode, creating missing parent directories
criteria.contract: the resulting tree holds the path as a blob with those bytes and that mode (`100644` when none is given); with mode `120000` the content is the link target

setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go, a table {put new/deep/f.txt content 'x' -> blob 'x' mode 100644; put a.txt content 'new' -> replaced, mode 100644; put img.bin content_base64 of bytes 00 ff 10 -> blob equals those bytes; put tool mode '100755' -> mode 100755; put link mode '120000' content 'a.txt' -> tree entry is a symlink whose target is 'a.txt'; put a.txt with its current content -> tree id equals the parent's tree id}: apply, then read back with git ls-tree -r and git cat-file blob

criteria.condition: a `delete`, `move` or `chmod` operation names an existing file (and, for `move`, a `to` that does not exist)
criteria.action: remove the path for `delete`, rename `from` to `to` keeping content and mode for `move`, and change only the mode for `chmod`
criteria.contract: the resulting tree lacks the deleted path; holds the moved file under `to` with the blob id and mode it had under `from`; holds the chmod-ed file with the same blob id and the new mode

setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go, a table {delete a.txt -> a.txt absent; delete docs/guide.md -> docs/ absent from the tree (no empty directory); move bin/run -> tools/run: tools/run has the old blob id and mode 100755, bin/run absent; chmod a.txt 100755 -> same blob id, mode 100755}: apply and compare git ls-tree -r output with the expected entries

criteria.action: for any list of operations, apply them one at a time in request order, each to the tree the previous one left
criteria.contract: `put a` followed by `delete a` leaves no `a`; a later operation may use a path an earlier one created or freed

setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib
check.pseudocode: in internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go, a table {[put a 'x', delete a] on a tree without a -> no a, tree equals the parent's; [delete a.txt, put a.txt 'z'] -> a.txt is 'z'; [put n 'x', move n -> m, chmod m 100755] -> only m, mode 100755; [move a.txt -> b.txt, put a.txt 'again'] -> both exist; [put d/f 'x', delete d/f, put d 'file'] -> d is a file}: apply and compare the tree

criteria.condition: an operation cannot apply to the tree as the earlier operations left it: `delete`, `move` or `chmod` of a missing path, `move` onto an existing path, `put` under a path that is a file, `put` onto a directory, or any operation on or under a submodule entry
criteria.action: refuse the whole request, naming the first operation that does not apply, and move no ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_operation` and `error.details.index` holding the zero-based index of that operation

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/ plus a submodule entry vendor/lib
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table of operation lists posted to the commit route with the failing operation at index 1 after one valid put {delete missing.txt; move missing.txt -> x; move a.txt -> bin/run (existing); move a.txt -> docs (a directory); chmod missing.txt 100755; put a.txt/child (a.txt is a file); put docs (a directory); put vendor/lib; delete vendor/lib; put vendor/lib/x}: assert status == 400; assert error.error_type == 'invalid_operation'; assert error.details.index == 1; assert the branch head is unchanged

criteria.condition: an operation is malformed: an unknown or missing `op`; a path that is empty, starts with `/`, has a `.` or `..` segment or a `.git` segment; a `put` with both or neither of `content` and `content_base64` or with invalid base64; a `put` mode outside `100644`, `100755`, `120000`; a `chmod` mode outside `100644`, `100755`; a missing field
criteria.action: refuse the request before resolving the parent
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the answer does not depend on the branch's state

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table of single operations {op 'copy'; no op; put with path ''; path '/abs'; path 'a/./b'; path 'a/../b'; path '.git/config'; path 'x/.git/hooks/h'; put with content and content_base64; put with neither; put content_base64 '!!!'; put mode '100600'; put mode '160000'; chmod without mode; chmod mode '120000'; move without to; delete without path}: assert 400 invalid_request for every row; the request carries a stale expected_head_sha and still answers 400, not 409

criteria.condition: the tree after all operations equals the parent's tree and `allow_empty` is absent or false
criteria.action: refuse the request and move no ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `empty_commit`; a request in which at least one operation changes the tree is accepted even when another operation changes nothing

criteria.condition: the request sets `allow_empty` to true
criteria.action: create a commit whose tree is its parent's tree
criteria.contract: HTTP 201; `commit.tree_sha` equals the parent's tree id

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/

requirements.title: Consequences of a commit
requirements.rationale: A commit through the API must be indistinguishable, afterwards, from a push of the same commit: same events, same versions, same changes.

criteria.condition: a commit request has moved or created its branch
criteria.action: emit one `parley.git.push` event and one `parley.scm.commit` event for the moved branch after the branch has moved and before answering
criteria.contract: `parley.git.push` with metadata `ref` (full name), `before` (null for a created branch), `after`, `created`, `deleted: false`, `forced: false`, `direct`, `via: "api"`; `parley.scm.commit` with metadata `branch`, `sha`, `parent_sha` and `files` (the paths the commit touched, both paths of a move, at most 100); both carry the request's `session_id` or null

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
a recording event sink behind the real event emitter interface
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commit_events_test.go: post a commit touching 3 paths (one of them a move a.txt -> b.txt) on existing branch work; assert the sink holds exactly [parley.git.push, parley.scm.commit]; push.metadata == {ref:'refs/heads/work', before: old, after: new, created:false, deleted:false, forced:false, direct:false, via:'api'}; commit.metadata.branch == 'work', sha == new, parent_sha == old, files == sorted paths incl. both a.txt and b.txt; post a commit creating branch n from base_ref -> push.before == null and created == true; post a commit with 150 puts -> len(commit.metadata.files) == 100

criteria.condition: a commit request has moved a branch that is the source of a `draft` or `open` change
criteria.action: have the ref-updated stage that package 22 registers with the ref writer of package 18 record a new version of kind `commit` at the new commit, in the store transaction of the ref update, and name the change and version in the answer
criteria.contract: `change` in the 201 answer is `{workspace_slug, number, version}`, the version the ref writer reports for the update; this package passes the version kind `commit`, the session and the caller's credential to the ref writer and makes no record call of its own

criteria.condition: a commit request on an unprotected branch carries a `change` object that passes the change component's checks
criteria.action: have the change component open a change with the request's `target_branch`, `title`, `intent` and `draft`, with the committed branch as source, and name it in the answer
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with `change` `{workspace_slug, number, version: 1}`; the change component is asked to check the opening before the branch moves and to open the change after it

criteria.condition: a commit or rebase request carries a `session_id` that the session linker (the interface SessionLinker of internal/scm, to which package 49 hands its session-linking check) does not accept for the caller and the workspace, or no session linker is registered
criteria.action: refuse the request and write nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `unknown_session`; no ref moves and no event is emitted; an accepted `session_id` appears on the emitted events and on any version recorded

criteria.condition: a `POST` to the commits, refs or rebase route repeats an `Idempotency-Key` that the same caller used on the same route for a request that succeeded within 24 hours, with the same body
criteria.action: answer with the recorded body of the first request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the first answer's body; no second commit, ref update or event; the same key with a different body answers HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict`

criteria.condition: a commit, ref create, ref move, ref delete or rebase request has moved a ref through the ref writer of package 18
criteria.action: leave the notification of the post-push listeners to that ref writer, to which it passed `via: "api"` and the request's `session_id`
criteria.contract: a listener registered with the ref writer of package 18 is called exactly once per accepted request with the workspace slug, the accepted update, via `api` and the request's session id, or null without one; the call comes from the event step of `Apply`; internal/scm holds no listener registry and calls no listener; a refused request causes no call

requirements.title: Push-rule refusals over the API
requirements.rationale: The API and the git server are two doors to one repository; a write refused over git must be refused here too, with a machine-readable type per rule.

criteria.action: for any ref update a write route is about to make, submit it to the push rule engine of package 18 (Evaluate in internal/gitserver/pushrule) with the caller facts, the full ref name, the `before` commit (none for a create) and the `after` commit (none for a delete), and make the update only when the engine accepts it, through the ref writer of the same package (Apply with via `api`)
criteria.contract: one evaluation per request, made before the compare-and-swap; the commit named as `after` exists in the repository when the engine is called; the compare-and-swap, the workspace's `head_sha`, the ref-updated stages and `parley.git.push` are the ref writer's, and this package has no second writer

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
a fake rule engine that records each evaluation and accepts
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rules_test.go, with a recording fake engine: a table {commit on existing branch -> (refs/heads/work, old, new); commit creating a branch -> (refs/heads/n, none, new); POST refs tag -> (refs/tags/v1, none, sha); PATCH ref -> (name, expected_sha, sha); DELETE ref -> (name, current, none); rebase -> (refs/heads/work, old, rebased head)}: assert exactly one engine call per request with those values and the request's credential; assert the call happened while rev-parse(ref) still returned the before value

criteria.condition: the push rule engine refuses the ref update of a write
criteria.action: refuse the request with the engine's message and the `error_type` of the refusing rule
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error.message` equal to the rule's message and `error_type` `hub_owned_ref` (rule 1), `protected_branch` (rule 2), `default_branch` (rule 2a), `tracking_branch` (rule 3), `integration_branch` or `patch_branch` (rule 4, by the kind of branch), `path_not_allowed` (rule 5)

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
a fake rule engine with scripted refusals
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rules_test.go, a table over the refusal the fake engine returns {rule hub-owned -> hub_owned_ref; rule protected -> protected_branch; rule default-branch -> default_branch; rule tracking -> tracking_branch; rule carry-patch on the integration branch -> integration_branch; rule carry-patch on a patch branch -> patch_branch; rule path -> path_not_allowed} crossed with the five write routes: assert status == 403; assert error.error_type as mapped; assert error.message == the engine's message verbatim (for example 'main is protected and cannot be force-pushed or deleted')

criteria.condition: a path-scoped PAT writes a commit that changes a file outside the token's `paths`
criteria.action: refuse the commit and name the first offending path
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `path_not_allowed` and the named member `error.path` holding the offending path

criteria.condition: a write names a tracking branch of a task fork
criteria.action: refuse the write and name the fork's base branch
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `tracking_branch` and `error.details.base_ref` equal to the fork's `fork_point.ref`

criteria.action: for any write the push rule engine refuses, leave every ref at its commit, emit no event and call neither the change component nor the idempotency record
criteria.contract: after a 403 push-rule refusal the output of `git for-each-ref` is byte-identical to before the request and no `parley.*` event exists for it

criteria.action: refuse the write and move no ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal`; the write is never accepted

requirements.title: Direct push through the API
requirements.rationale: The owner exemption must behave the same at both doors, or the API becomes a way around (or a stricter copy of) branch protection.

criteria.condition: the workspace's owner or the admin token, with a credential the owner exemption accepts and `protect.owner_push` true, creates a commit on a protected branch
criteria.action: accept the commit as a direct push, mark the push event as direct and open no change and record no version for the branch
criteria.contract: HTTP 201; `parley.git.push` has `direct: true`; `change` and `change_error` are null; when the branch is the default branch the workspace's `head_sha` equals the new commit

criteria.condition: a commit on a protected branch comes from a caller or credential the owner exemption does not cover: the owner's workspace-bound PAT, the owner's path-scoped PAT, or any caller while `protect.owner_push` is false
criteria.action: refuse the commit and leave the protected branch where it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `protected_branch` and the fast-forward message of rule 2

criteria.condition: a commit request on a protected branch carries a `change` object
criteria.action: refuse the request before resolving the parent or writing any object
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for every caller that passes the write gate; no object is written

criteria.action: accept the update as a direct push
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; `parley.git.push` has `direct: true` and `forced: false`; no version is recorded

requirements.title: Ref create, move and delete
requirements.rationale: Review and revert tooling needs to make and remove branches and tags without a clone, under the same compare-and-swap discipline as commits.

criteria.condition: `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs` carries a valid `name` that does not exist and exactly one of `sha` and `ref`, resolving to a commit
criteria.action: create the ref at the named commit and emit one `parley.git.push` event with `created: true`
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the ref object; a bare `name` creates `refs/heads/<name>`; a tag is lightweight

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_write_test.go, a table {name 'x', sha full id of main -> refs/heads/x, kind branch; name 'refs/heads/feat/y', ref 'main' -> refs/heads/feat/y; name 'refs/tags/v1', ref 'main' -> kind tag; name 'z', ref a 7-character abbreviation -> created}: assert 201; assert r.json.name, r.json.kind, r.json.sha == main head; assert git rev-parse <full name> == main head; assert git cat-file -t refs/tags/v1 == 'commit' (a lightweight tag); assert the sink holds one parley.git.push with before == null, after == sha, created == true, via == 'api'

criteria.condition: a ref creation request is invalid: `name` is missing, is not a valid git ref name, is `HEAD`, or lies outside `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/` and `refs/parley/`; both or neither of `sha` and `ref` are given; `sha` is not a full 40-character id; the target resolves to no commit; or the ref already exists
criteria.action: refuse the request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a bad name or target field; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for a target that resolves to no commit; HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_exists` for an existing ref; a name under `refs/parley/` answers HTTP 403 with `error_type` `hub_owned_ref`

setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_write_test.go, a table {no name; name ''; name 'a..b'; name 'x.lock'; name 'refs/heads/'; name 'refs/notes/n'; name 'refs/remotes/o/m'; name 'HEAD'; both sha and ref; neither; sha of 7 characters; sha not hexadecimal} -> 400 invalid_request; {sha 40 hex naming no object; sha naming a tree; ref 'nope'} -> 404 ref_not_found; {name 'main'; name 'refs/heads/main'} -> 409 ref_exists; {name 'refs/parley/changes/1/1'} with the real rule engine -> 403 hub_owned_ref: assert for-each-ref unchanged in every row

criteria.condition: `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name` names an existing unprotected branch or a tag, by full name or by branch name, with a `sha` that is a commit of the repository and an `expected_sha` equal to the ref's commit
criteria.action: move the ref to `sha` by compare-and-swap and emit one `parley.git.push` event whose `forced` is true exactly when the old commit is not an ancestor of the new one
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the ref object at `sha`; a move to the commit the ref already has answers 200 and emits no event; a branch that is the source of a `draft` or `open` change gets a version of kind `ref`, recorded by the ref-updated stage of package 22 from the version kind this route passes to the ref writer

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_write_test.go, a table addressed once as '/scm/refs/work' and once as '/scm/refs/refs/heads/work' {sha a descendant of work -> forced false; sha the parent of work -> forced true; sha a sibling commit -> forced true; a tag refs/tags/v1 moved -> 200; sha equal to the current commit -> 200 and no event}: assert 200 and r.json.sha == sha; assert rev-parse; assert the event's before, after, forced, created == false, via == 'api'; with the recording stage registered: assert it was called once per moved ref with via 'api' and version kind 'ref'

criteria.condition: a ref move names a ref that does not exist, omits `sha` or `expected_sha`, gives a `sha` that is not a full id of a commit in the repository, or gives an `expected_sha` that differs from the ref's commit
criteria.action: refuse the move and leave the ref where it is
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_moved` and `error.details.current_sha` for a mismatch; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for a missing ref or a `sha` naming no commit; HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a missing or abbreviated field

criteria.condition: `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name` names an existing unprotected, non-default branch that is not a change's source, or a tag, with no `expected_sha` or one equal to the ref's commit
criteria.action: delete the ref by compare-and-swap against its current commit and emit one `parley.git.push` event with `deleted: true`
criteria.contract: HTTP 204; the ref no longer exists

requirements.title: Server-side rebase
requirements.rationale: An agent keeps its branch current with the target without fetching, and gets a conflict as data when it cannot (SCM-US-05).

criteria.condition: `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase` names a branch that has commits not in `onto`, where `onto` is not an ancestor of the branch head, and the replay applies without conflict
criteria.action: replay those commits in order on top of the commit `onto` resolves to, keeping each commit's author and message and setting the hub as committer, move the branch to the result by compare-and-swap and emit one `parley.git.push` event
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{status: "rebased", branch, old_head_sha, new_head_sha, onto_sha, change}`; `branch` is the ref object at `new_head_sha`; the event has `forced: true` when the old head is not an ancestor of the new one

setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rebase_test.go: r = post('/workspaces/w/scm/rebase', {branch:'topic', onto:'main', expected_head_sha: T2}); assert 200; assert r.json.status == 'rebased'; old_head_sha == T2; onto_sha == M2; new_head_sha == rev-parse(topic) != T2; branch.sha == new_head_sha; change == null; assert git rev-list --count main..topic == 2 and merge-base(main, topic) == M2; assert the two new commits keep the authors and messages of T1 and T2 and have the hub as committer; assert git diff T1^ T1 equals the diff of the first new commit; assert one push event {before: T2, after: new, forced: true, via:'api'}; a second row without expected_head_sha -> 200

criteria.condition: a rebase request names an `onto` that is an ancestor of the branch head or equal to it
criteria.action: answer without moving the branch and without emitting an event
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `status` `up_to_date` and `new_head_sha` equal to `old_head_sha`

setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rebase_test.go, a table over onto {M1 (an ancestor of topic), T2 (the head itself), 'topic'}: assert 200, status == 'up_to_date', old_head_sha == new_head_sha == T2, onto_sha == the resolved commit; assert rev-parse(topic) == T2 and the sink is empty and the rule engine was not called

criteria.condition: a rebase request names a branch whose every commit is already contained in `onto`, by ancestry or because each replayed commit changes nothing
criteria.action: move the branch to the `onto` commit
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `status` `rebased` and `new_head_sha` equal to `onto_sha`

setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rebase_test.go, a table {branch behind at M1, onto main -> new_head_sha == M2, event forced false; branch whose two commits were cherry-picked onto main as M3, M4, onto main -> new_head_sha == M4, event forced true}: assert 200 and status == 'rebased'; assert rev-parse(branch) == rev-parse(main)

criteria.condition: a commit of the branch does not apply on top of `onto`
criteria.action: abandon the rebase, leave the branch at its old head and report the conflict
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `rebase_conflict` and `error.details` holding the conflict report, the type ConflictReport of internal/gitrepo that package 20 declares (`target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha`, `files` with `path`, `kind`, `base`, `ours`, `theirs`, `landed_by`; `landed_changes`; `change`); no ref moves, no event is emitted and no temporary file of the rebase remains

setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1), with a conflicting edit of a.txt on both sides
a recording event sink
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/rebase_test.go: M2 and T1 both change line 1 of a.txt; r = post rebase {branch:'topic', onto:'main'}; assert 409; assert error.error_type == 'rebase_conflict'; d = error.details; assert d.target_sha == M2, d.head_sha == T2, d.base_sha == M1, d.commit_sha == T1; assert d.files == [{path:'a.txt', kind:'content', base, ours, theirs each with sha, mode and path, landed_by: []}]; assert d.landed_changes == [] and d.change == null; assert rev-parse(topic) == T2; assert the sink is empty; assert the repository directory holds no leftover worktree, index or lock file created by the request; a modify/delete conflict reports kind 'modify_delete' with theirs or ours null on the side that lacks the file

criteria.condition: a rebase request is invalid: `branch` or `onto` is missing, `branch` is not an existing branch, `onto` resolves to no commit, or the commits to replay include a merge commit
criteria.action: refuse the rebase and move nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `merge_commits_unsupported` for a merge commit in the range; HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a missing field or a `branch` that is not under `refs/heads/`; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for an unknown branch or `onto`

setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)

criteria.condition: a rebase request's `expected_head_sha` differs from the branch head, or the branch moves between the read of its head and the compare-and-swap
criteria.action: refuse the rebase and keep the other writer's head
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_moved` and `error.details.current_sha`; the branch stays at the commit the other writer gave it

a recording event sink

criteria.condition: a rebase has moved a branch that is the source of a `draft` or `open` change
criteria.action: have the ref-updated stage of package 22 record a version of kind `rebase` at the new head, in the store transaction of the ref update, and name the change and version in the answer
criteria.contract: `change` in the 200 answer is `{workspace_slug, number, version}`

a recording ref-updated stage registered with the ref writer of package 18 in place of package 22's, which reports a scripted version for the moved branch; a fake change linker registered in place of package 22's that records its calls and returns scripted answers

requirements.title: CLI commands for commit and rebase
requirements.rationale: A person or a script commits local files and rebases a branch from a shell with one command each.

criteria.condition: `parley scm commit <slug>` runs with `--branch`, `--message`, `--expected-head` and any number of `--put <repo-path>=<local-file>`, `--delete <repo-path>` and `--move <from>=<to>` flags
criteria.action: send one `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` whose `operations` follow command-line order, with each `--put` file's bytes as `content_base64`, and print the hub's answer
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds the hub's 201 body as one JSON document; `--base` is sent as `base_ref`

criteria.condition: `parley scm commit` runs without `--expected-head`
criteria.action: read the branch with `GET /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name` first and send the `sha` it returns as `expected_head_sha`
criteria.contract: the ref read precedes the commit request; a `404 ref_not_found` from the read means a new branch and the commit request is sent without `expected_head_sha`; any other error from the read is printed and ends the command with exit code 1

criteria.contract: the `change` member is present exactly when at least one of `--change-target`, `--title`, `--intent`, `--draft` is given, and holds only the members whose flags were given

criteria.condition: `parley scm commit` or `parley scm rebase` is run without a required flag or argument, with a `--put` or `--move` value that lacks `=` or has an empty side, or with a `--put` local file that cannot be read
criteria.action: fail before sending any request
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr holds the error envelope with `code` 0 and `error_type` `usage_error`; nothing on stdout; no HTTP request is sent

criteria.condition: the hub answers `parley scm commit` or `parley scm rebase` with an error, such as `409 ref_moved` or `409 rebase_conflict`
criteria.action: print the hub's error envelope as received and stop without retrying
criteria.contract: exit code 1; stderr holds the envelope with its `details` (the current head, or the conflict report); nothing on stdout; exactly one write request was sent

execution_paths.title: An agent commits edits to its fork without a clone and is told when the branch moved

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<fork>/scm/commits with a fork-bound PAT, branch greeting, base_ref main, a message and three operations (two puts and a delete)
passes the write gate, validates the body, resolves main in the fork and applies the operations to its tree
creates the commit, has the push rule engine accept the creation of refs/heads/greeting and creates the branch by compare-and-swap
emits parley.git.push (created, via api) and parley.scm.commit and answers 201 with the commit and the branch
reads GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork>/scm/file?ref=greeting&path=api/greeting.go and receives the bytes it put
fetches the fork over /git and sees refs/heads/greeting at the commit the API answered
posts a second commit to greeting with expected_head_sha set to main's head
answers 409 ref_moved with details.current_sha equal to the first commit and leaves greeting where it is

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server and its check pipeline
the write gate and commit handler of internal/scm
internal/gitrepo running the git binary on a bare repository
the push rule engine of package 18
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
a registered workspace cloned from a local origin repository made with git init, and a task fork of it with a fork-bound PAT holding git:read and git:write
end_state: refs/heads/greeting exists in the fork at the commit the first answer named, with one parent equal to main's head
the file route returns the put content at ref greeting
a stock git ls-remote of the fork lists refs/heads/greeting at that commit
the event log holds one parley.git.push with via api and created true and one parley.scm.commit for the branch, and none for the refused second request
the second request was answered 409 ref_moved with the first commit as current_sha
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: r = POST commits {branch:'greeting', base_ref:'main', message, operations:[put api/greeting.go, put docs/g.md, delete api/old.go]}; assert r.status == 201; sha = r.json.commit.sha; assert GET file(ref greeting, api/greeting.go).body == content; assert exec('git ls-remote <hub>/git/<org>/<fork>.git refs/heads/greeting') starts with sha; r2 = POST commits {branch:'greeting', expected_head_sha: mainHead, ...}; assert r2.status == 409 and r2.json.error.details.current_sha == sha; assert GET /events/log filtered to the fork lists parley.git.push then parley.scm.commit once each

execution_paths.title: A developer commits a local file and rebases the branch from the shell

steps.action: runs parley scm commit <slug> --branch topic --base main --message 'Add notes' --put notes.md=./notes.md
reads GET …/scm/refs/topic, receives 404 ref_not_found, and sends POST …/scm/commits with base_ref main and the file as content_base64
creates the commit and the branch topic and answers 201
prints the answer on stdout and exits 0
after another commit reached main, runs parley scm rebase <slug> topic --onto main
sends POST …/scm/rebase with branch topic and onto main
replays the commit of topic onto main's head, has the push rule engine accept the non-fast-forward move, moves topic by compare-and-swap and emits parley.git.push with forced true
prints the answer with status rebased and exits 0

real_components: the parley CLI root command and its HTTP client
the commit, ref and rebase handlers of internal/scm
the push rule engine of package 18
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
a registered workspace owned by the developer, whose API key is in PARLEY_API_KEY
a local file notes.md in t.TempDir()
main is not protected in this workspace (protected_branches set to an empty list) so a second commit can be put on main through the API
end_state: topic holds exactly one commit ahead of main and its parent is main's current head
notes.md at ref topic has the local file's bytes
the first command printed a document with commit and branch; the second printed status rebased with old_head_sha different from new_head_sha
the event log holds a parley.git.push for topic with forced true and via api
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: out1, code1 = runCLI('scm','commit',slug,'--branch','topic','--base','main','--message','Add notes','--put','notes.md='+local); assert code1 == 0 and json(out1).branch.name == 'refs/heads/topic'; POST commits on main (other file) with the owner key; out2, code2 = runCLI('scm','rebase',slug,'topic','--onto','main'); assert code2 == 0; j = json(out2); assert j.status == 'rebased' and j.onto_sha == main head and j.new_head_sha != j.old_head_sha; assert GET compare(base main, head topic).ahead == 1 and .behind == 0; assert GET file(topic, notes.md) == local bytes

execution_paths.title: The owner pushes directly to a protected branch through the API and other credentials cannot

steps.action: as the workspace's owner, sends POST …/scm/commits with an API key, branch main and main's head as expected_head_sha
builds the commit and submits the fast-forward update of the protected branch to the push rule engine, which accepts it under the owner exemption
moves main, updates the workspace's head_sha, emits parley.git.push with direct true, opens no change and answers 201 with change null
sends the same kind of request to main with the owner's workspace-bound PAT and the new head as expected_head_sha
answers 403 protected_branch with the rule's message and leaves main where the owner put it
sends a commit request for main with an API key
answers 403 forbidden at the write gate, because a member has read access only, and moves nothing

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server and its check pipeline
the commit and ref handlers of internal/scm
the push rule engine of package 18 with the owner exemption
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
a registered workspace in an organization, with default settings (main protected, protect.owner_push true)
its owner's API key, a PAT of the owner bound to the workspace with git:write, and the API key of a second user who is a member of the organization
end_state: main is at the owner's commit and the workspace record's head_sha equals it
the event log holds exactly one parley.git.push for refs/heads/main, with direct true and via api
no change exists whose source is main
the bound PAT's commit request was answered 403 with error_type protected_branch and the member's was answered 403 with error_type forbidden
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: r = POST commits as owner {branch:'main', expected_head_sha: head, message, operations:[put CHANGELOG.md]}; assert r.status == 201 and r.json.change == null; assert GET /workspaces/<slug>.head_sha == r.json.commit.sha; ev = events of type parley.git.push for refs/heads/main; assert len(ev) == 1 and ev[0].metadata.direct == true; r2 = POST commits with the owner's bound PAT and expected_head_sha == r.json.commit.sha; assert r2.status == 403 and r2.json.error.error_type == 'protected_branch'; r3 = the same request with the member's API key; assert r3.status == 403 and r3.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert GET /scm/refs/main .sha == r.json.commit.sha
